summary: Vague report: jobs sit in the queue and are never picked up although a worker is running. No version, broker, command or logs given.

Written in Spanish. Enqueueing PDF invoices as base64 job arguments fails with ORB-1202 PayloadTooLarge (702 KB against the 512 KB limit); the reporter asks whether the limit can be raised and how to pass large files to a job.
Vague report: all scheduled cron jobs have run one hour early since Sunday with no change on the reporter's side. No version, schedules or time zone given.

Written in Hindi. Under Docker Compose the worker fails at startup with ORB-1001 BrokerConnectionError connecting to localhost:6379, although the Redis container is running and ORBIT_BROKER_URL is redis://localhost:6379/0; the reporter asks whether a port must be opened.
Feature request: Orbit CLI commands such as `orbit doctor` print ANSI colour codes into CI logs; they should honour NO_COLOR and skip colour when stdout is not a TTY.
Vague report: workers stop processing jobs after some hours and recover when restarted. No version, logs or setup given.

Written in Portuguese. Upgrading from 2.9 to 3.0.0 on Kubernetes where all configuration lives in ORBIT_* environment variables: `orbit migrate-config` only reads orbit.ini and the worker now ignores the variables, so the reporter asks how to write orbit.toml and for a variable-to-key mapping.
On 3.0.0, adding the documented `[limits] max_payload_kb` key to orbit.toml makes workers refuse to start with ORB-1802 UnknownConfigKey, and `orbit doctor` reports the same unknown key.

When a flow step times out on every attempt (ORB-1502 StepTimeout) and goes to the DLQ (ORB-1301), `orbit flows status` keeps showing the step and the run as running instead of failed, with the next step pending instead of skipped.

After raising `heartbeat_seconds` to 120 with `lease_seconds` at 300, `orbit doctor` fails its worker check; the reporter asks what the heartbeat <= lease/3 rule protects against and whether it is safe to ignore for short jobs.
Written in German. On 3.0.3 a schedule with a named day-of-week range (`30 6 * * MON-FRI`) fails with ORB-1401 ScheduleParseError, while single day names and the numeric range 1-5 work.
On 3.1.0 `orbit doctor` prints a failed results check (ORB-1601 ResultBackendUnavailable) yet ends with 'All checks passed.' and exits 0, so CI misses the misconfiguration; 3.0.3 exited 1.
On a managed Redis with `maxmemory-policy volatile-lru`, some enqueued jobs silently vanish: they never run and never reach the DLQ, while Redis reports thousands of evicted keys.

After a planned Redis failover on 3.1.0, 40 worker pods reconnect with no jitter, Redis hits maxclients at 100% CPU, and workers log a flood of ORB-1001 BrokerConnectionError for about 14 minutes until scaled down.

On 3.1.2 a job that sets `backoff=` in its decorator ignores the global `[retries] max_delay_seconds` cap again, with retry delays up to 3311 s before ORB-1301 RetryExhausted; the reporter calls it a regression of #128.
The valid cron step-over-range expression `0 9-17/2 * * MON-FRI` is rejected at import time with ORB-1401 ScheduleParseError.
A 7-9 minute nightly export intermittently runs twice: the first attempt logs ORB-1101 LeaseExpired and a second worker starts the job, with `lease_seconds = 300` and `heartbeat_seconds = 240`.
Vague report: the dashboard shows only a blank white page and nothing appears in the logs. No version or setup given.
Inside a Python 3.12 virtualenv, the first line of `orbit doctor` reports the system interpreter (python 3.9.6) instead of the interpreter Orbit is running on.
ORB-1201 SerializationError messages still contain the full repr() of non-serializable object arguments, leaking customer PII into logs; the 3.0.0 fix in #85 only covered dict arguments.

Written in Japanese. A six-field cron expression with a seconds field (`0 0 9 * * *`) fails with ORB-1401 ScheduleParseError; the reporter asks whether seconds are supported and how to run at 09:00 JST on UTC servers.

`orbit doctor` reports every check as OK, but every Flow run fails with ORB-1601 ResultBackendUnavailable because the app role lacks grants on the result tables; the reporter wants the results check to touch the backend.
After upgrading to 3.2.0, OIDC sign-in to the dashboard behind a TLS-terminating nginx loops until the browser stops with ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS, and the dashboard logs ORB-1701; 3.1.2 worked.
Since upgrading to 3.2.0, worker RSS grows linearly on a queue with `prefetch = 500` until ORB-2101 WorkerOOM kills the worker about every 4 hours; on 3.1.2 memory was flat.
Vague report: nothing works after upgrading Orbit, with nothing else changed. No versions, errors or details given.
Feature request: ORB-1901 BrokerRateLimited log lines, and ideally the throttling metric, should include the SQS queue name and MessageGroupId so the hot FIFO queue can be found without CloudWatch.
Docs request: state clearly that Orbit has no job-cancel operation and document the cancelled-flag pattern for delayed jobs, linking the cancel feature request (#34).
Vague report: on 3.2.0 some scheduled jobs sometimes run at the wrong time. No schedules, examples, time zone or logs given.
Very long, log-heavy report on the 3.2.0 Postgres broker: about 5 s pickup latency spikes with two causes, nightly listener connection resets logged as ORB-1001 and NOTIFY events missed under load.
Feature request: show each running job's last-heartbeat age in the dashboard workers view, highlighted past lease_seconds/3, so imminent lease expiry (ORB-1101) is visible.
